explanation: An area in the ancient Middle East that includes parts of today's Israel, Palestine, Lebanon and Syria. It was the destination of the Israelites' journey after they left Egypt.
A people descended from the patriarch Jacob (also called Israel). They became slaves in Egypt before God led them out under Moses' leadership.
A central figure in Judaism, Christianity and Islam. He led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Ten Commandments from God on Mount Sinai.
A staff with a bronze serpent that Moses made according to God's instruction. When the Israelites were bitten by poisonous snakes, they could look at this staff and be healed.
An ancient kingdom south of the Dead Sea, inhabited by the Edomites, who were descendants of Esau, Jacob's brother.
A Canaanite king who attacked the Israelites and took some of them captive.
A city in Canaan that the Israelites destroyed as revenge for Arad's attack.
